scroll_title: The Mystery of the Eden Tree
clue: I stand in the middle of the Garden. Whoever eats my fruit will know good and evil. God commanded Adam and Eve not to eat from me. What am I?
options: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
correct_answer: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil
fact: God commanded Adam and Eve not to eat from this specific tree in the Garden of Eden.

clue: I was the very first human born on earth, but out of jealousy because God accepted my brother's offering over mine, I took his life. Who am I?
fact: Cain attacked his younger brother Abel in the field, becoming the first murderer.

clue: When a global flood submerged the earth, I was built with three decks of gopher wood and preserved eight human lives and the animal kingdom. What am I?
fact: Noah built the Ark exactly to God's dimensions over many years of faithful labor.

clue: After the great Flood, God placed me in the clouds as an everlasting covenant token that He would never again destroy the earth by water. What am I?
fact: God set His bow in the clouds as a reminder of His mercy and enduring covenant.

clue: When prideful humanity attempted to build a tower reaching to the heavens, God confused their language at this famous ancient city. Which city was it?
fact: The Lord confused the language of the whole world at Babel and scattered people over the earth.

clue: As fire and brimstone rained down upon Sodom, who disobeyed the angels' warning by looking back and was turned into a pillar of salt?
fact: Lot's wife looked back at Sodom with longing and became a pillar of salt.

clue: Though my brothers sold me into slavery in Egypt, God gave me wisdom to interpret Pharaoh's dreams and I became ruler over all Egypt. Who am I?
fact: Joseph saved Egypt and his entire family from a severe seven-year famine.

clue: I burned with fire yet was not consumed. From my midst, God called Moses to return to Egypt and liberate His people. Where was I located?
fact: The angel of the Lord appeared to Moses in flames of fire from within a bush at Horeb.

clue: When the destroying angel passed through Egypt, what blood was painted on the doorposts so the firstborn inside would be spared?
options: The blood of a Passover lamb
correct_answer: The blood of a Passover lamb
fact: 'When I see the blood, I will pass over you,' the Lord promised His people.

clue: When Moses stretched out his staff, which mighty body of water divided to create a dry path for Israel and drowned the Egyptian army?
fact: The Lord drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land.

clue: Falling like dew each morning in the wilderness, what white, coriander-like substance tasted like wafers made with honey?
fact: The Israelites ate manna for forty years until they reached the border of Canaan.

clue: On which holy mountain did God Himself write the Ten Commandments on two stone tablets and give them to Moses?
fact: God gave Moses two tablets of the covenant law, inscribed by the finger of God.

clue: While Moses delayed on Mount Sinai, what idolatrous image did Aaron fashion out of gold jewelry for the Israelites to worship?
fact: They bowed down to the calf and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of Egypt.'

clue: I am overlaid with gold, and inside me lie the golden jar of manna, Aaron's staff that budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant. What am I?
fact: The Ark of the Covenant rested in the Most Holy Place as the throne of God's presence.

clue: Which woman in Jericho hid the Israelite spies and tied a scarlet cord in her window so her household would be spared?
fact: By her faith, Rahab and all her family were saved when Jericho fell.

clue: After marching around the city for seven days and blowing ram's-horn trumpets on the seventh day, which city's walls collapsed flat?
fact: When the trumpets sounded and the people shouted, the walls of Jericho fell.

clue: When Joshua prayed during battle, 'Sun, stand still over Gibeon,' for about how long did the sun delay going down?
fact: The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day.

clue: Armed only with trumpets, clay jars, and torches, which judge defeated the vast Midianite army with just 300 men?
fact: They shouted, 'A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!' and God granted the victory.

clue: I tore a young lion apart with my bare hands. My supernatural strength was tied to my Nazarite vow and uncut hair. Who am I?
fact: The Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon Samson, giving him miraculous strength.

clue: 'Your people will be my people and your God my God.' Which Moabite woman spoke these words to her mother-in-law Naomi?
fact: Ruth's loyalty led her to Bethlehem, where she became an ancestor of King David and Jesus.

clue: Who was the wealthy landowner in Bethlehem who showed kindness to Ruth as she gleaned in his field and later married her?
fact: Boaz acted as kinsman-redeemer, marrying Ruth and becoming the great-grandfather of David.

clue: 'Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.' Which boy prophet heard God calling him in the night while sleeping in the tabernacle?
fact: Samuel grew up to be Israel's greatest judge and the prophet who anointed Saul and David.

clue: Armed with only a shepherd's staff, a sling, and five smooth stones from a stream, who killed the Philistine giant Goliath?
fact: 'I come against you in the name of the Lord Almighty,' David declared to Goliath.

clue: Though I was King Saul's eldest son and heir, I loved David as my own soul and gave him my royal robe, sword, and bow. Who am I?
fact: Jonathan made a solemn covenant of friendship with David and protected him from Saul.

clue: When the Ark of the Covenant was brought into Jerusalem, which king danced before the Lord with all his might wearing a linen ephod?
fact: David rejoiced with uncontained gratitude at God's holy presence entering Jerusalem.

clue: When God appeared in a dream and asked, 'Ask for whatever you want,' which young king asked for a discerning heart to govern God's people?
fact: God was so pleased with Solomon's request that He also granted him riches and honor.

clue: Who spent seven years building the magnificent first Temple of the Lord on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem?
fact: Upon completion, the glory of the Lord filled the Temple in a thick cloud.

clue: Which royal visitor traveled a great distance with spices, gold, and jewels to test King Solomon with hard questions?
fact: She exclaimed to Solomon, 'Not even half was told me; you far exceed the report I heard!'

clue: During a three-and-a-half-year drought, which prophet was fed bread and meat every morning and evening by ravens at the Kerith Ravine?
fact: God miraculously commanded the ravens to sustain Elijah during the national famine.

clue: On which mountain did God send down fire from heaven to consume Elijah's water-drenched sacrifice before 450 prophets of Baal?
fact: When all the people saw it, they fell prostrate and cried, 'The Lord—He is God!'

clue: Who was separated from Elisha by a chariot and horses of fire and taken up to heaven in a whirlwind without dying?
fact: Elisha picked up Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him and received a double portion of his spirit.

clue: Which Syrian army commander was healed of leprosy after Elisha told him to wash seven times in the Jordan River?
fact: When Naaman dipped seven times, his flesh was restored clean like that of a young boy.

clue: Because I continued praying three times a day toward Jerusalem despite a royal decree, I was cast into the lions' den. Who am I?
fact: God sent His angel to shut the mouths of the lions, and Daniel was found completely unhurt.

clue: Who were the three Hebrew young men thrown into a fiery furnace for refusing to worship King Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue?
fact: A fourth figure looking like the Son of God walked with them in the flames, and they were unharmed.

clue: Fleeing God's command to preach in Nineveh, which prophet was swallowed by a huge fish and spent three days and nights inside its belly?
fact: When Jonah repented and prayed from inside the fish, it vomited him out onto dry land.

clue: 'The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures.' Who composed this beloved psalm?
fact: Psalm 23 is the most cherished song of comfort and trust in God's pastoral care.

clue: 'Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path.' In which chapter of Psalms is this famous verse found?
fact: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible, devoted to celebrating God's holy law.

scroll_title: The Shelter of the Most High
clue: 'Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.' Which psalm begins with this promise?
fact: Psalm 91 is renowned as the ultimate prayer of divine protection in times of danger.

clue: 'The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.' Which book of wisdom opens with this motto?
fact: Written primarily by Solomon, Proverbs offers timeless practical wisdom for righteous living.

clue: 'Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.' Where is this famous proverb found?
fact: In all your ways submit to Him, and He will make your paths straight.

clue: 'Meaningless! Meaningless! Everything is meaningless!' Who wrote Ecclesiastes after examining all human pursuits under the sun?
fact: Ecclesiastes concludes that the whole duty of humanity is to fear God and keep His commandments.

clue: 'He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; by His wounds we are healed.' Which prophet wrote this?
fact: Isaiah 53 foretold the sacrificial death of Jesus Christ seven centuries before His crucifixion.

clue: As prophesied by Micah, in which town of Judea was Jesus Christ, the Bread of Life, born?
fact: Bethlehem means 'House of Bread' in Hebrew, fitting for the birthplace of the Bread of Life.

clue: Which archangel appeared to Mary in Nazareth saying, 'Do not be afraid, Mary; you have found favor with God'?
fact: Gabriel told Mary that her son Jesus would reign over Jacob's descendants forever.

clue: Following the star in the east to Bethlehem, what three symbolic treasures did the Magi present to baby Jesus?
fact: Gold symbolized royalty, frankincense signified priesthood, and myrrh foreshadowed His burial.

clue: Keeping watch over their flocks at night, to whom did the angel of the Lord first announce the birth of the Savior?
fact: The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger.

clue: Warned by an angel in a dream that King Herod sought to kill baby Jesus, to which country did Joseph flee with his family?
fact: They remained in Egypt until Herod's death to fulfill the prophecy, 'Out of Egypt I called my son.'

clue: After returning from Egypt, in which town of Galilee did Jesus grow up, fulfilling the word, 'He will be called a Nazarene'?
fact: Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man while living in Nazareth.

clue: At age twelve, where was Jesus found after three days of searching, sitting among the teachers listening and asking questions?
fact: 'Didn't you know I had to be in my Father's house?' Jesus asked His parents.

clue: Who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River to fulfill all righteousness?
fact: John initially hesitated, saying, 'I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?'

clue: As Jesus came up out of the water at His baptism, in what form did the Holy Spirit descend upon Him?
fact: A voice from heaven said, 'This is my Son, whom I love; with Him I am well pleased.'

clue: Where was Jesus led by the Spirit immediately after His baptism to fast for forty days and be tempted by the devil?
fact: After fasting forty days and forty nights, Jesus was hungry when the tempter came to Him.

clue: When Satan tempted Jesus to turn stones into bread, what did Jesus say man must live on instead of bread alone?
options: Every word that comes from the mouth of God
correct_answer: Every word that comes from the mouth of God
fact: Jesus defeated every temptation of Satan by quoting the Scripture, 'It is written...'

clue: 'Come, follow me, and I will send you out to fish for people.' Who were the first two fisherman brothers Jesus called?
fact: At once they left their nets by the Sea of Galilee and followed Him.

clue: I was sitting at the tax collector's booth when Jesus said, 'Follow me.' I left my table and wrote the first Gospel. Who am I?
fact: Matthew hosted a great dinner at his house where Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners.

clue: After spending the whole night in prayer on a mountainside, how many of His disciples did Jesus choose and name Apostles?
fact: The twelve apostles represented the foundation of the New Testament church.

clue: At which village wedding did Jesus perform His first miracle by transforming six stone jars of water into choice wine?
fact: This first sign revealed His glory, and His disciples put their faith in Him.

clue: How many barley loaves and small fish from a boy's lunch did Jesus bless to feed five thousand men?
fact: Everyone ate until satisfied, and the disciples gathered twelve basketfuls of leftovers.

clue: During the fourth watch of the night, which disciple stepped out of the boat and walked on the stormy Sea of Galilee toward Jesus?
fact: When Peter saw the wind he grew afraid and began to sink, crying, 'Lord, save me!'

clue: Awakened from sleep during a furious squall on the lake, who commanded the wind and waves, 'Quiet! Be still!'?
fact: The wind died down and it was completely calm, leaving the disciples in utter awe.

clue: Who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years and was healed instantly upon touching the fringe of Jesus' cloak?
fact: 'Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace,' Jesus told her.

clue: When Jesus cleansed ten men with leprosy, of what nationality was the only man who returned to glorify God at Jesus' feet?
fact: Jesus asked, 'Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?'

clue: At the Pool of Bethesda in Jerusalem, whom did Jesus cure by commanding, 'Get up! Pick up your mat and walk'?
fact: At once the man was cured; he picked up his mat and walked on the Sabbath day.

clue: Who had been dead and buried in a cave in Bethany for four days when Jesus called out in a loud voice, 'Come out!'?
fact: The dead man came out, his hands and feet wrapped with strips of linen.

clue: Taking a twelve-year-old girl by the hand, who said, 'Talitha koum,' which means, 'Little girl, I say to you, get up!'?
fact: Immediately the twelve-year-old girl stood up and began to walk around.

clue: Touching an open funeral coffin at the town gate of Nain, who raised a weeping widow's only son back to life?
fact: 'Young man, I say to you, get up!' Jesus said, and the dead man sat up and began to talk.

clue: Jesus made mud with saliva, anointed a man born blind, and sent him to wash in which pool in Jerusalem to receive his sight?
fact: Siloam means 'Sent'; the man went and washed, and came home seeing.

clue: Sitting by the roadside near Jericho, who shouted, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' and received his sight?
fact: Throwing his cloak aside, Bartimaeus jumped to his feet and came to Jesus.

clue: 'Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.' Which officer in Capernaum showed faith that amazed even Jesus?
fact: 'I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith,' Jesus commended him.

clue: How many friends made an opening in the roof of a crowded house in Capernaum to lower their paralyzed friend down to Jesus?
fact: Seeing their faith, Jesus forgave the man's sins and commanded him to walk.

clue: Who wasted his father's inheritance in a distant land, ended up feeding pigs, and returned home to a joyful father's embrace?
fact: The father ran, embraced him, and ordered the finest robe and ring for his son who was lost and found.

clue: When a traveler was beaten by robbers and left half dead, who took pity on him after a priest and a Levite passed by on the other side?
fact: He bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, and paid for his care at an inn.

clue: In the Parable of the Sower, which seed produced a crop thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times what was sown?
options: The seed sown on good soil
correct_answer: The seed sown on good soil
fact: Good soil represents those who hear the word, understand it, and bear fruit in righteous living.

clue: In the wedding parable, how are the five bridesmaids described who brought jars of oil along with their lamps for the bridegroom?
fact: Those who were ready went in with the bridegroom to the wedding banquet.

clue: In the Parable of the Talents, which servant was rebuked because he was afraid and hid his master's one talent in the ground?
fact: God expects us to faithfully invest and use the gifts and resources He entrusts to us.

clue: Who left ninety-nine sheep in the open country to search for the one lost sheep until he found it and carried it home on his shoulders?
fact: There is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons.

clue: Who lay covered with sores at a rich man's gate desiring crumbs, and after dying was carried by angels to Abraham's side?
fact: In eternity, Lazarus was comforted in peace while the rich man suffered in torment.

clue: During the Last Supper, who poured water into a basin and washed His disciples' feet as an enduring example of humble service?
fact: 'I have set you an example that you should do as I have done for you,' Jesus taught.

clue: Who went to the chief priests asking, 'What are you willing to give me if I deliver Him over to you?' and accepted thirty silver coins?
fact: From then on Judas watched for an opportunity to hand Jesus over to them.

clue: In the Garden of Gethsemane, who prayed in such anguish, 'Not my will, but yours be done,' that His sweat fell like drops of blood?
fact: An angel from heaven appeared to Jesus in Gethsemane and strengthened Him.

clue: Which three disciples fell asleep from sorrow in Gethsemane when Jesus asked them to keep watch and pray with Him?
fact: 'Watch and pray so that you will not fall into temptation,' Jesus urged them.

clue: Leading a crowd with swords and clubs into Gethsemane, who identified Jesus to the arresting soldiers by greeting Him with a kiss?
fact: 'Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?' Jesus asked.

clue: 'I do not know the man!' Who denied knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crowed, and then wept bitterly in repentance?
fact: Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken, and he went outside and wept bitterly.

clue: Which Roman governor declared, 'I am innocent of this man's blood,' and washed his hands before the crowd while condemning Jesus?
fact: Pilate had Jesus flogged and handed Him over to be crucified to satisfy the crowd.

clue: By what Aramaic name, meaning 'The Place of the Skull,' was the hill outside Jerusalem called where Jesus was crucified?
fact: Golgotha is translated Calvary in Latin, marking the site of Christ's sacrifice.

clue: As Jesus was led out to be crucified, whom did Roman soldiers compel to carry the wooden cross behind Him?
fact: Simon of Cyrene was the father of Alexander and Rufus, known in the early church.

clue: Mocking Jesus as 'King of the Jews,' what painful crown did Roman soldiers twist together and press onto His head?
fact: They put a reed in His hand, knelt before Him, and mocked His royal identity.

clue: 'Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.' To which repentant person hanging on a cross did Jesus promise Paradise?
options: The repentant thief on the right
correct_answer: The repentant thief on the right
fact: 'Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise,' Jesus promised him.

clue: What triumphant final three-word shout did Jesus utter on the cross as He completed our redemption before bowing His head?
fact: In Greek, 'Tetelestai' means 'Paid in Full'—the debt of sin was fully satisfied.

clue: At the moment Jesus died on the cross, what sacred barrier in the Temple was torn in two from top to bottom?
fact: The torn curtain signified that access to the Most Holy Place of God was open to all through Christ.

clue: Which wealthy secret disciple asked Pilate for Jesus' body, wrapped it in clean linen, and laid it in his own new rock-hewn tomb?
fact: Joseph rolled a big stone in front of the entrance to the tomb and went away.

scroll_title: He Is Not Here, He Is Risen
clue: Whose appearance was like lightning with clothing white as snow when he rolled away the tomb stone and announced Christ's resurrection?
fact: 'He is not here; He has risen, just as He said. Come and see the place where He lay.'

clue: Weeping at the empty tomb on Easter morning, who turned and cried out 'Rabboni!' as the first witness of the risen Lord Jesus?
fact: Jesus told Mary Magdalene to go to His brothers and declare His resurrection.

scroll_title: Unless I See the Nail Marks
clue: Which apostle said, 'Unless I see the nail marks in His hands and put my finger where the nails were, I will not believe'?
fact: Eight days later Jesus appeared and invited Thomas to touch His wounds.

clue: Upon seeing the risen Christ and His wounds, who exclaimed the great confession of faith, 'My Lord and my God!'?
fact: 'Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed,' Jesus responded.

clue: To which village seven miles from Jerusalem were two disciples walking when Jesus joined them and revealed Himself in the breaking of bread?
fact: They said to each other, 'Were not our hearts burning within us while He talked with us on the road?'

clue: For how many days after His resurrection did Jesus appear to His disciples, speaking about the kingdom of God before His ascension?
fact: He gave many convincing proofs that He was alive during those forty days.

clue: 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel to all creation.' By what name is this final missionary command of Jesus known?
fact: Jesus commanded His followers to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching them.

clue: From which famous mountain near Jerusalem did Jesus ascend into heaven while two white-robed angels promised His return?
fact: He was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.

clue: On the Day of Pentecost, what appeared like tongues of fire resting on each of the 120 believers in the upper room?
fact: All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues.

clue: Which apostle preached with boldness on Pentecost, proclaiming the crucified and risen Christ so that 3,000 people were baptized that day?
fact: Peter proclaimed, 'Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ!'

clue: 'Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!' Who was healed?
fact: He jumped to his feet and began to walk, entering the temple courts walking and leaping and praising God.

clue: Which husband and wife sold a piece of property but lied about the proceeds to the Holy Spirit, falling dead instantly at Peter's feet?
fact: Great fear seized the whole church and all who heard about these tragic events.

clue: Looking up into heaven while being stoned to death, who prayed, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them,' as the first Christian martyr?
fact: Stephen saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

clue: Who was sent by an angel to a desert road to explain the prophet Isaiah to an Ethiopian eunuch riding in his chariot and baptize him?
fact: When they came up out of the water, the Ethiopian went on his way rejoicing.

clue: Traveling to Damascus to persecute Christians, who was blinded by a light from heaven and heard Jesus say, 'Saul, why do you persecute me?'?
fact: Saul was transformed from the greatest persecutor of the church into its greatest apostle.

clue: Which believer in Damascus laid hands on blind Saul so that something like scales fell from his eyes and he was filled with the Spirit?
fact: Ananias addressed him as 'Brother Saul,' and Paul was baptized immediately.

clue: Who knelt down and prayed in Joppa, saying, 'Tabitha, get up,' bringing a godly woman who made garments for the poor back from the dead?
fact: Tabitha opened her eyes, and seeing Peter she sat up; this became known all over Joppa.

clue: While Peter preached in Caesarea, which Roman centurion and his household became the first Gentiles to receive the Holy Spirit?
fact: Peter declared, 'God does not show favoritism but accepts from every nation those who fear Him.'

clue: In which Syrian city were the disciples of Jesus called 'Christians' for the very first time in history?
fact: Barnabas and Paul met with the church at Antioch for a whole year and taught great numbers.

clue: Sleeping between two soldiers bound with two chains, who was struck on the side and freed from Herod's prison by an angel at night?
fact: The iron city gate opened for them by itself, and Peter returned to the praying church.

clue: Singing hymns to God in a Philippian prison at midnight, which two missionaries experienced an earthquake that broke every prisoner's chains?
fact: The Philippian jailer asked, 'Sirs, what must I do to be saved?' and was baptized with his household.

clue: 'For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that whoever believes in Him shall not perish.' Where is this verse?
fact: John 3:16 is often called 'The Gospel in a Nutshell' for its concise message of salvation.

clue: 'For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.' Who wrote these words to Rome?
fact: Eternal life is a free gift of God's grace, not something earned by human effort.

clue: 'In all things God works for the good of those who love Him, who have been called according to His purpose.' Where is this promise?
fact: God sovereignly weaves even trials and hardships together for the ultimate good of His children.

clue: 'Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.' Which famous chapter of 1 Corinthians is this?
fact: And now these three remain: faith, hope and love. But the greatest of these is love.

clue: Where in the New Testament are the nine fruit of the Spirit listed—love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control?
fact: Against such virtues there is no law; they are produced by the Holy Spirit in a believer's life.

clue: 'For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God.' Where is this found?
fact: Salvation is entirely God's gift, not by works, so that no one can boast.

clue: Which chapter of Ephesians instructs believers to put on the belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shield of faith, and helmet of salvation?
fact: The sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God, is our offensive weapon against the enemy.

clue: 'I can do all this through Him who gives me strength.' In which epistle of encouragement did Paul pen this verse?
fact: Paul wrote these words while imprisoned in Rome, testifying to Christ's sustaining power.

clue: 'Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!' Which letter is celebrated as Paul's 'Epistle of Joy'?
fact: Despite chains and adversity, Paul mentions joy and rejoicing sixteen times in Philippians.

clue: 'Rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.' Where is this found?
fact: A lifestyle of prayer and gratitude keeps a believer aligned with God's will.

clue: 'All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness.' Where is this written?
fact: The Holy Scriptures equip the servant of God thoroughly for every good work.

clue: 'Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.' Which chapter is known as the 'Hall of Faith'?
fact: Hebrews 11 honors Old Testament heroes like Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Rahab for their faith.

clue: 'And without faith it is impossible to please God, because anyone who comes to Him must believe that He exists.' Where is this found?
fact: God rewards those who earnestly and sincerely seek Him in faith.

clue: 'Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.' In which chapter of Hebrews is this reassuring truth recorded?
fact: While earthly circumstances change, Christ's character, mercy, and promises endure forever.

clue: 'As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.' Which New Testament writer emphasized living faith?
fact: James taught that genuine saving faith naturally produces good works and loving actions.

clue: 'Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Come near to God and He will come near to you.' Where is this?
fact: Our spiritual victory comes through humility before God and active resistance against Satan.

clue: 'But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession.' Which apostle wrote this identity description?
fact: We are chosen to declare the praises of Him who called us out of darkness into His wonderful light.

clue: 'Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour.' Who warned believers to be alert and sober-minded?
fact: Peter exhorts believers to stand firm in the faith against the enemy's schemes.

clue: 'If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.' Where is this?
fact: The blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from every sin when we humbly confess.

clue: 'God is love... There is no fear in love. But perfect love drives out fear.' Which apostle wrote these famous words on divine love?
fact: Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them.

clue: 'This is the victory that has overcome the world, even our faith. Who is it that overcomes the world? Only the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God.'
fact: Faith in Jesus Christ as the Son of God is our ultimate victory over worldly darkness.

clue: Exiled to a rocky island because of the word of God, who was in the Spirit on the Lord's Day and wrote the Book of Revelation?
fact: John was exiled to the island of Patmos where he saw the triumphant glorified Christ.

clue: 'I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.' Who declares this eternal sovereignty?
fact: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, symbolizing eternity.

clue: 'Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person.' Where is this?
fact: Jesus desires personal, intimate communion with every heart and church that opens to Him.

clue: The heavenly New Jerusalem does not need the sun or the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and who is its lamp?
fact: In God's eternal city, the presence of Christ the Lamb illuminates everything in pure glory.

clue: 'He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.' Where is this eternal promise found?
fact: The old order of suffering and death will pass away forever in God's new creation.

clue: Standing on each side of the river of the water of life is the Tree of Life, bearing twelve crops of fruit. For what are its leaves used?
options: For the healing of the nations
correct_answer: For the healing of the nations
fact: The Tree of Life from Eden is restored in the New Jerusalem for eternal blessing.

clue: What is the very last verse of the entire Holy Bible (Revelation 22:21)?
options: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with God's people. Amen.
The Lord bless you and keep you. Amen.
May the peace of God guard your hearts forever.
To Him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
correct_answer: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with God's people. Amen.
fact: The Bible concludes with a benediction of God's amazing grace to all His people.
